newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-QUIRKY FIFA SOCCER COLLECTION LAUNCHED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-QUIRKY FIFA SOCCER COLLECTION LAUNCHED.

text.p: A quirky FIFA collection tracing the origins of soccer back 3,000 years to China was launched at the world's biggest book fair on Wednesday.

Sports fanatic Harry Langton has donated 2,000 pieces of soccer memorabilia to the International Football Federation which are being featured at the mobile international exhibition before finding a permanent home in England.

"Football had a past before but never had a documented history" said Dr Frank Braun, Berlin publisher of "The FIFA Museum Collection", in an interview. "Football does not belong to one nation. It is a global heritage. About 500 million people now play it around the world,"
But why has soccer become the world's most popular sport?
"It is like a modern war game emotionally. We haven't got wars anymore and we need soccer to release those emotions," Braun said.

"The origins of the game go back to Asia so it is very appropriate that the World Cup is being staged in Korea and Japan in 2002. That is a modern renaissance, taking the game back to where it started."
The collection begins with Chinese paintings of ceremonial football games and an elegantly flowing Chinese character whose symbol means "To kick with one foot".
Nothing is too trivial for the collection -- from cigarette cards of football heroes of old to leather bottle balls that used to be kicked around English village greens.
The shock of women first taking to the soccer pitch is captured by a shocked and chauvinistic newspaper account of a Scottish match played in Edinburgh in 1881:

"So it has come at last. What next? Several years ago there was a rage for silly displays of certain kinds of athletics by women but we thought the time had passed for another outburst in the form of Association Football."
